first.rationale: The two measured declines (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) are upstream of revenue and are the failure mode most directly addressed by inherited evidence: memory_86 (shorter onboarding lifted completion and time-to-value) and memory_31 (signup simplification produced a durable SMB activation lift) point the same direction, and memory_91 suggests the activation funnel is responsive generally. I verify memory_86 because it is the direct basis for the chosen action and I want to see whether the reported lift was in completion only or carried through to retained, revenue-relevant adoption. I verify memory_73 because promotional pricing is the intuitive answer to the competitor's entry pricing but its readout self-flags a mid-test cohort redefinition with pooled results; if that pooling inflated the effect, the whole price-match direction is weaker than it looks, and even if real, discount-acquired price-sensitive SMBs are the cohort most likely to churn or repriced-renew poorly \u2014 a direct threat to the sustainable long-term qualified revenue objective rather than headline acquisition. I explicitly do not treat the inherited memories as settled: memory_86 and memory_31 measured lifts in a different competitive environment and against a healthier baseline, so a lift observed then may not reproduce now, and completion/activation gains are proxies that may not convert into qualified revenue. Referral incentives (memory_57) act on established customers and do not touch the observed decline; enterprise sales-assist (memory_44) is plausible but addresses a segment that is not where the deterioration or the competitive pressure is. Standard experiment scale with a proper holdout, tracking activation and completion as primary but instrumenting downstream retention and revenue quality so the result is interpretable beyond the proxy. If verification shows memory_86's lift was completion-only with no adoption follow-through, I would shift to activation_messaging as the narrower intervention.
